title: when the brief cites an owner decision key, have ork run adj check on it and say in the brief when it is not found

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The reviewer reported this as tool feedback (deterministic-check) on ork in ork run ork-20261125-153910-3562, project ork, item S557:

when the brief cites an owner decision key, have ork run adj check on it and say in the brief when it is not found

Evidence: feedback.direction-duplicates is cited as an owner decision but adj check returns not found, per the implementer report

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: `internal/engine/brief.go` (owner-decision annotation), `internal/engine/round.go` (owner-decision section assembly), `internal/engine/brief_test.go` (brief integration tests), `docs/design.md` (brief behavior), and `landed-changed/S566.md` via slicer.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: `internal/engine/brief_test.go`: TestOwnerDecisionKeyChecksReachBriefs asserts missing keys are annotated in actual role briefs; decided, open and closed keys add no line. Markers outside the Owner decisions paragraph and keys carrying an adj id are not checked.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: In the Owner decisions paragraph written by RecordSpecAnswers (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:833-847`), recognize only `[key]` and `[key, adj N]` markers. When adding the Owner decisions brief section in runRound (`internal/engine/round.go:663-675`), run adj check for keys without an adj id. Append "adj check KEY: not found" for missing keys; found keys add no line. Do not re-check keys carrying adj N. Use the existing adj client. Document this behavior and add the slice changelog entry. Owner answer: owner-decisions, 2026-11-25, brief.decision-key-check; tighten the Files, Failing tests, Implement and Check sections.
